html:
The week of Thanksgiving, the phone calls we get from Fountain Inn sound alike: relatives are coming from out of state, the house has not had a real clean since summer, and nobody wants to spend the holiday weekend scrubbing a shower. If that is your week, this checklist gives you a realistic order of work, a countdown, and a clear idea of what to hand off.

Fountain Inn is a good example of why holiday prep varies. Homes near the walkable Main Street are often older, with smaller kitchens that work hard on a feast day. The newer neighborhoods off I-385 and SC-418 tend to have open floor plans where the kitchen, dining and living room all show at once. Both layouts reward the same approach: clean what guests see and touch first.

Count back from guest day

Trying to do everything the day before is how people end up wiping counters at midnight. Break it into stages instead.

Ten days out

  • Clear the guest room closet and make room for coats and suitcases.
  • Wash guest bedding and any throw blankets that sat out all summer.
  • Take down summer decor and wipe the shelves underneath it.

Four days out

  • Dust ceiling fans, vents and the tops of cabinets, since dust falls and you want it down before you mop.
  • Clean windows and sliding door glass on the inside.
  • Do the oven now. A self-clean cycle smells for hours, and you do not want that on the day you bake.

Day before

  • Bathrooms: toilet, sink, mirror, shower, fresh towels.
  • Vacuum and mop everything.
  • Empty the refrigerator of what is old to make room for leftovers.

The three places guests actually notice

After years of cleaning before holidays, the team has a short list of where hosts get judged. The first is the guest bathroom, specifically the base of the toilet, the faucet and the mirror. The second is the entryway floor, because red clay and wet leaves come in on every shoe in November. A runner or a quick mop by the door pays back all weekend. The third is the kitchen counters and stovetop; if those shine, the rest of the house reads as clean.

What guests almost never notice is the inside of your drawers or the back of your closets. Skip them this week and put the time toward floors, baseboards and glass.

How much does one time house cleaning cost in Fountain Inn?

This is the question behind most holiday calls, and we answer it the same way every time. Perfect Services does not give a price by phone or photo. After a free in-home estimate, a short visit where we walk through the rooms with no commitment, you get an exact number. The factors that matter are:

  • Home size: square footage and the number of rooms to work through.
  • Condition: a home kept up through the fall is a lighter job than one that was skipped.
  • Add-ons: oven, refrigerator, inside windows or cabinets.
  • Date: the days right before Thanksgiving and Christmas fill first.
  • Pets: hair on upholstery and floors adds time.

The details of what a single visit includes are on the one-time house cleaning service page, and you can start an estimate from the one time cleaning in Fountain Inn page.

How long it takes and when to book

A typical Fountain Inn home takes a two-person team several hours for a full one-time clean, longer if the oven and the refrigerator are included. That is why the week before a holiday is hard to book, and why asking early matters. If you are reading this with a few days left, send a message and ask what is open; sometimes there is room after another visit wraps up. Be careful about promising yourself a specific slot until the estimate is done, because we confirm dates after seeing the home.

Hosting an Airbnb or renting a room over the holidays

If you host paying guests too, the checklist grows by a restock list and a fresh set of linens, and our holiday checklist for Moore hosts walks through that side. For neighbors one town over, one-time cleaning in Simpsonville works the same way. If your home needs more than a surface clean, a deep cleaning adds baseboards, grout and cabinet fronts. Our fall one-time cleaning guide covers the leaf-and-mud problem in more detail.

What to do with the kitchen on the day itself

Thanksgiving and Christmas dinners put more strain on the kitchen than any other day of the year. Before you start cooking, empty the dishwasher, wipe the counters and clear the sink, so there is room to put dirty pans as you go. Keep a bowl of hot soapy water by the stove for spills, and run a first load of dishes as soon as the oven timer starts. A trash can with a fresh liner near the prep area saves a dozen trips across the room. The next morning, the stovetop and oven door are the first things to wipe while the mess is still soft; if it sits for a few days, the grease hardens and the job doubles.

A short pre-guest walk-through

Before the doorbell rings, stand at the front door and look at the house like a first-time visitor. Does the entry floor look clean? Is the guest bath fresh? Is the trash out of the kitchen? Fix those three and you are ready. The Brazilian detail-first method we use at Perfect Services is basically that walk-through done room by room, with the finish check from the doorway.

faqs: Can I book a one-time cleaning right before Thanksgiving in Fountain Inn?
Sometimes. The week before a holiday fills first, so ask early. We confirm dates after the free in-home estimate.
Should I deep clean or do a one-time clean before guests arrive?
If you have not had a thorough clean in months, a deeper visit helps with baseboards and grout. For a home kept up, a one-time clean is usually enough.
What should I do before the cleaners arrive?
Pick up clutter, put away personal items and tell us about any areas that need extra attention. We handle the cleaning itself.
